desc: Formalize expansion/closure rule; prove per-K closure is a unique maximal interval and the family of intervals is laminar.
Analyze decreasing/increasing DSU activation approaches; show both fail (smaller-later absorption and spurious intervals) — reject DSU-activation approach.
Derive correct structural recursion: max-Cartesian tree, equal-value right-spines, qualifying maxima, strict promotion rule (touching segment-root sum > M), degenerate all-equal forests.
Design O(N) implementation: Cartesian tree via monotonic stack, iterative post-order, per-primary-node combine, DSU-style promotion links with path compression for answers.
Implement the full Python solution per NOTES (fast I/O, no deep recursion, 64-bit-safe sums).

Verify implementation: run both samples for exact match; brute-force stress-test on random small arrays with heavy duplicates and edge patterns; fix any mismatches (check middle-segment promotion lB/rB and qualifying-max condition first).
Final complexity/edge-case review: N=5e5 performance, equal adjacent values, K=1/N endpoints, all-equal array, strictly increasing/decreasing arrays.
